The morning will run as follows:
9.00am-9.45am – tour of school
9.45am-10.30am – talk in the hall with Mrs Kirby (Headteacher) and Mrs Moss (Deputy Headteacher)
To book a place please email office@warnhamprimary.co.uk or call 01403 265230
Welcome to Warnham CE Primary School!
We have great pleasure in welcoming you to Warnham CE Primary School, situated at the heart of the peaceful village of Warnham, just outside of Horsham.
Our village school benefits from close ties with St Margaret’s church and brims with energy and life. Visitors often comment on what a happy place it is! We are part of a close knit community, where Governors, parents and village residents support the school and an active PTFA organises numerous fun-filled events through-out the year.
We love our school and hope you enjoy finding out more about us. Thank you.
We are proud to be a teacher training partnership school. For more information use the following link https://www.inspiringfutureteachers.org/tanbridge
“Warnham is a happy, friendly place. Pupils are polite and kind to one another and behave well… High expectations for what pupils can achieve are evident in the strong achievement of pupils…Values of ‘Thankfulness’, ‘Love’ and ‘Courage’ underpin this close-knit school community…Behaviour in the school is a strength…Relationships underpin the atmosphere of warmth and esteem found throughout the school. ”
Ofsted Inspection Report, Nov 2024

Governors
The governing body plays an important strategic role by giving direction and focus on the governance of the school.
Their role is to govern rather than manage. This includes:
> Promoting high standards of education > Planning the school’s long-term future > Overseeing the school’s aims, values and ethos > Ensuring proper financial management of the school > Appointing staff, including the headteacher > Communicating openly with parents, the local community and the local education authority > Supporting the school
The full governing body meets at least once a term and has two committees who discuss issues in greater detail and report back to the main meetings. The two committees cover Resources & Finance and Ethos & Curriculum. There is also a Holiday Request panel who meet when the need arises.
The governing body of Warnham School is made up of 12 governors:
> 4 Co-opted governors – appointed by the governing body after considering the skills and experience they can bring to the role > 3 Foundation Governors – appointed by the Diocese > 1 Local Authority Governor – appointed by the Local Authority > 2 Parent Governors – elected by parents/carers of pupils at the school > 1 Staff Governor – elected by the staff of the school > 1 Headteacher – an ex-officio member by virtue of the post
Safeguarding
Our Safeguarding governor is Mrs Hilary Farquhar.
Details of serving governors 2026-27
Shirley Kirby is the Headteacher who took up post on 1 January 2018. By virtue of her position she is an ex-officio member of the governing body and attends all the meetings of the main committees.
Hilary Farquhar is a Co-opted Governor who has served on the governing body since September 2009, originally as a Community Governor. She is co-Chair of Governors, and a member of the Resources & Finance committee and the Ethos & Curriculum committee. She has special responsibility for Safeguarding and monitors the Maths curriculum. She sits on the Holiday Requests panel.
Marlene Fleming is a Co-opted Governor who was originally appointed on 17 September 2018. She is co-Chair of the Governors and is a member of the Resources & Finance committee and the Ethos & Curriculum committee. She has special responsibility for monitoring SEND, disadvantaged students and the PSHE and RSHE curriculum.
Allison Goodfellow is a Co-opted Governor appointed on 14 September 2022. She is Chair of the Ethos & Curriculum committee and has special responsibility for EYFS and Assessment.
Ian Gurling is a Parent Governor who was re-elected on 2 February 2024. He is chair of the Resources & Finance committee. He has special responsibility for Health & Safety and E-safety and for monitoring the Computing curriculum.
Rachel Hamer is a Foundation Governor who was originally appointed on 26 July 2017. She serves on the Resources & Finance committee. She also monitors the Humanities, Music and MFL curriculums.
Gytha Hodgson has served on the governing body since March 2008 as the Local Authority Governor. She is Vice Chair of Governors and serves on the Resources & Finance committee and the Ethos & Curriculum committee. She is a member of the Holiday Requests panel. She is also a Governor representative of the Parents Teacher & Friends Association.
Rev Rebecca Tuck is a Foundation Governor who took up post as priest in charge of St Margaret’s Church on 23 September 2021. She is a member of the Ethos & Curriculum committee and monitors the RE curriculum.
Rhiannon Ho is a Parent Governor who was appointed on 20 September 2024. She serves on the Resources & Finance Committer and monitors the English curriculum.
Lucy Hammond is a Staff Governor who was elected on 22 May 2025.
Debbie Ladds is a Co-opted Governor who was appointed on 3 December 2025. She serves on the Resources & Finance Committee and monitors the Science curriculum.
Retirements in 2025/2026
Luke Davies was a Foundation Governor who resigned on 22 July 2026.

Our Aims for Each Child at Warnham
INDEPENDENCE
To nurture independent, responsible, life-long learners equipped with creative thinking skills to enable them to respond to the challenges of the world they live in.
CO-OPERATION
To support pupils to understand that their co-operation with adults and their peers leads to a fulfilling and collaborative learning environment.
MOTIVATION
To provide creative and exciting learning opportunities for pupils to relish their learning opportunities as well as developing their own work ethic in becoming self-motivated learners.
PERSEVERANCE
To empower pupils to become confident in making decisions, be able to take risks and persevere to allow them to challenge their learning and maximise their potential.
CURIOSITY
To create an environment of curiosity to encourage pupils to want to know more and how to develop the necessary skills to fulfil their desire to learn.
CREATIVITY
To foster a love of the arts, provide pupils with opportunities to express themselves creatively and use these skills to help them to problem solve across all aspects of their learning.
FOREST SCHOOL
Our school is surrounded by beautiful fields and woodland and we are delighted that the children can take full advantage of this in their regular Forest School sessions. They are able to walk from school, with our fully trained forest school leader, Mrs Lunnon, straight into the woods and spend a whole morning or afternoon learning in a woodland environment. If you would like to read more about this, please have a look at our handbook.
CORE AND FOUNDATION SUBJECTS
All children are taught the core subjects of English, Mathematics and Science and wherever possible this is integrated into the themed topic along with the foundation subjects. Religious Education is an important area of the curriculum and is taught either through the creative curriculum or as a separate lesson.
These subjects are taught wherever possible within our topics. We follow National Curriculum guidelines, full details can be found HERE. For Reception Class we follow the EYFS Curriculum guidelines available HERE.
We have a daily phonics session in our Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and Key Stage 1 classes following the ‘Song of Sounds’ scheme. This scheme provides a synthetic and systematic approach to the teaching of phonics and supports both the development of children’s reading and writing skills. Children in Key Stage 2 also have a daily phonics / spelling session. Children are taught as a whole class to ensure all children hear, learn and have experience of the phonics programme for their year group. Some children benefit from additional overlearning, consolidation and practise at other times supported by highly skilled adults.
In Key Stage 1, spellings are based on the current week’s teaching and contain both tricky and decodable words. In Key Stage 2, weekly spellings are linked to the spelling rules and patterns that are being taught in addition to topic words or words that are commonly misspelt.
Parents are key partners in our approach to phonics and spelling and are invited into school during the first academic year to take part in their child’s phonic sessions as well as given guidance on how to support their children at home.
EYFS CURRICULUM
At Warnham CE Primary School our EYFS provision, practise and curriculum reflects the needs of the children in the class. Our team are quick to respond to the children’s interests and their progress is supported by a passionate and knowledgeable team. Learning happens through play, experiences, songs and stories both indoors and outside. The adults learn alongside the children to support thinking, develop knowledge and to support children in taking the next step.
Each day we have an interactive phonics session which carefully builds the skills needed for reading and writing following the Song of Sounds progression.
Our curriculum is based on the seven areas of learning and founded in the four key principles of the EYFS: a unique child, an enabling environment, positive relationships and learning and development.

Welcome to Warnham CE Primary School
We have great pleasure in welcoming you to Warnham CE Primary School which is situated within the peaceful village of Warnham just outside of Horsham. Warnham CE Primary School has a strong reputation for its kind and nurturing ethos whilst striving for excellence in children and staff alike. Our Christian values of Thankfulness, Love and Courage underpin all of our play and learning at Warnham.
Our Mission Statement ‘Let your light shine’ taken from Matthew 5:16 focuses on our strong belief that all children are individuals and need to be inspired and supported to achieve their best. We make the most of their talents and further develop their learning to help children to be proud of who they are, all they have accomplished and excited for their future.
We bring the curriculum alive with themed days, school trips, guest speakers and even sleepovers, enriching the experiences for the children and maximising their learning potential. We encourage every child to work hard, to co-operate and collaborate with others, to take pride in their own and others’ achievements and to be proud of our school.
We are a ‘Voluntary Controlled’ School meaning the Church of England maintains an active interest in the school whilst giving overall control to the Local Authority.
We welcome visits to our school and look forward to sharing our learning community with you.
Shirley Kirby Head Teacher
“Parents and carers are highly positive about the work of the school. They have ‘nothing but praise’ for the work of staff. They note how their children ‘thrive’ as a result of ‘well trained, kind and caring staff’ and ‘would never consider any other school.“
Ofsted Inspection Report, Nov 2024
Warnham CE Primary Vision and Values
“Let your light shine” Matthew 5:16
Our Values
THANKFULNESS for every opportunity whilst practicing humility as we aspire to learn and experience all that is yet to be discovered.
“Always give thanks for everything.” Ephesians 5:20
LOVE for one another, the world God has created for us, our learning and ourselves as we aim to flourish as a community.
“Let us be concerned for one another, to help one another to show love and do good.” Hebrews 10:24-25
COURAGE to embrace and overcome obstacles as we endeavour to achieve excellence both in ourselves and in challenging injustice through shining a light for others.
“Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged (for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go). Joshua 1:9
Our Vision
Warnham CE Primary is a deeply nurturing school at the heart of our village community. As a Church of England school, we celebrate diversity and inclusion, welcoming children and their families equally, regardless of their faith or religious beliefs. We aim to challenge and strive for excellence in all that we do guided by our Christian ethos and our core Christian values of Thankfulness, Love and Courage.
Our ambition is that our children will flourish by ‘Letting our Light Shine’, becoming humble, loving and courageous citizens who demonstrate thankfulness for each moment and all that they are yet to discover, just as Jesus did. We are passionate about unlocking the wonders of aspirational learning, developing skills in our children of co-operation, perseverance, independence, motivation, curiosity, and creativity. It is our goal that throughout their lives, our school community will embrace life in all its fullness whilst empowering others to do the same.

Our Community
As a church school, we are also proud of our link to our local church and community with the vicar playing an active role in school worship. The children and teachers regularly attend services at St Margaret’s Church including a termly School Communion. Our Christian ethos underpins everything that we do as a school. https://www.warnhamchurch.co.uk/
Warnham is a thriving and pretty village set in leafy West Sussex in the heart of the countryside. There is a strong community spirit with a thriving parish church, a pre-school, toddler group and the WI to name a few plus small businesses such as a village store and butcher.
The village comes together for many events and has enjoyed royal celebration street parties, cricket fun days, church bazaars and of course, school events such as the Fireworks Display and the Summer and Christmas fairs where everyone is welcome. We use our lovely hall for many of these events as this and the associated facilities are available for hire by the wider community.
We are committed to ensuring that we play an active part in the wider community that surrounds our school as well as enabling our children to contribute to and become responsible citizens in society.
“The school’s values of ‘thankfulness’, ‘love’ and ‘courage’ underpin this close-knit school community. Pupils live these out daily and celebrate when they demonstrate these traits. Pupils understand having the ‘courage’ to ‘try new things and persevere when things are tough’. They explained how important it is to ‘stand up for others’.”
Ofsted Inspection Report, Nov 2024
Warnham Bambies is a small baby & toddler group who meet in St Margaret’s Parish Room every Wednesday. Once a month, the rural toy library visit with a selection of their toys from the bus.
